display_title: [XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate A2A+GEMM and GEMM+A2A splitting in WindowedEinsumHandler.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate A2A+GEMM and GEMM+A2A splitting in WindowedEinsumHandler.

Extract `WindowedEinsumVisitor::SplitA2aGemmAlongContractingDim` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/windowed_einsum_handler.cc` to share the contracting-dimension splitting logic between `HandleDot` (A2A+GEMM) and `HandleAllToAll` (GEMM+A2A).

The two implementations were identical except for:
- Which instruction is the root of the pattern (`dot` for A2A+GEMM vs. `a2a` for GEMM+A2A), used for the output buffer shape and final `ReplaceInstruction` call.
- Which LHS tensor is sliced in each split (`a2a->mutable_operand(0)` for A2A+GEMM vs. `dot->mutable_operand(0)` for GEMM+A2A).
- The shape and ordering of the per-split `all-to-all` and `dot` instructions (`all-to-all` with `lhs_slice_shape` followed by `dot` for A2A+GEMM vs. `dot` followed by `all-to-all` with `a2a->shape()` for GEMM+A2A).

Release notes

Sourced from lit's releases.

LLVM 23.1.4 Release

  • Linux x86_64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Linux Arm64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64): xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows x64 (64-bit): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows on Arm (ARM64): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.4-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. The .tar.zst files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where LLVM-*.msi is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive clang+llvm- contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. You most likely want the LLVM- installer, unless you are developing software which itself uses LLVM, in which case choose clang+llvm-.

In addition, source archives are available:

  • To get all the llvm-project source code for this release, choose llvm-project-23.1.4.src.tar.xz.
  • test-suite-23.1.4.src.tar.xz is an archive of the LLVM Test Suite) for this release.

Verifying Packages

All packages come with a matching .sig and/or .jsonl file. You should use these to verify the integrity of the packages.

If it has a .sig file, it should have been signed by the release managers using GPG. Download the keys from the LLVM website, import them into your keyring and use them to verify the file:

$ gpg --import release-keys.asc
$ gpg --verify <package file name>.sig <package file name>

If it has a .jsonl file, use gh to verify the package:

$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name>
(if you are able to connect to GitHub)
$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name> --bundle <package file name>.jsonl
(using attestation file on disk)

display_title: **Status quo**

head_commit.message:
**Status quo**
`CudnnScaledDotHelper::IsSupported` requires both `lhs` and `rhs` contracting dimensions of `kScaledDot` to be the minor dimension (`rank - 1`, i.e., `NT` layout), and `GpuLayoutAssignment` assigns the default `{1, 0}` layout to all four `kScaledDot` operands. When `lhs` or `rhs` has contracting dimension `0` (`NN`, `TN`, or `TT`), `NVPTXCompiler::IsScaledDotSupportedByBackend` rejects the instruction during `ScaledDotRewriter`, decomposing `kScaledDot` into an upcast and BF16 `dot`.

**Why**
Falling back to decomposed BF16 `dot` on `NN`, `TN`, and `TT` loses 1.5x to 5.0x throughput on Blackwell B200 compared to native cuDNN block-scaled GEMM (`__cudnn$fusion`). Both fixed `{1, 0}` entry parameter layouts and unconstrained `AUTO` entry parameter layouts need to lower to `__cudnn$fusion` across `MXFP8`, `MXFP4`, and `NVFP4`.

**Design choices**
- Relax pre-fusion `CudnnScaledDotHelper::IsSupported(scaled_dot, /*is_fused=*/false)` in `NVPTXCompiler::IsScaledDotSupportedByBackend` so `ScaledDotRewriter` preserves `NN`, `TN`, and `TT` `kScaledDot` instructions before layout assignment.
- Add `GpuLayoutAssignment::AddScaledDotBackendConstraints` to set minor-contracting layouts on `lhs`, `rhs`, `lhs_scale`, and `rhs_scale` via `SetDotOperandLayoutToMinorContracting` when `!xla_gpu_experimental_scaled_dot_with_triton()`. For `AUTO` entry layouts, `{0, 1}` propagates to entry parameters with zero runtime data transposes; for fixed `{1, 0}` entry layouts, `LayoutAssignment` inserts `kCopy` to `{0, 1}`.
- Add `LayoutNormalization::HandleScaledDot` to absorb non-default-layout `kBitcast` operands and update `dot_dimension_numbers()` so both contracting dimensions become `rank - 1` (`NT`) before `SubByteNormalization`.
- Prevent `GemmFusion` from fusing `kTranspose` into `kScaledDot` fusions when `!xla_gpu_experimental_scaled_dot_with_triton()`, keeping `kScaledDot` operands as fusion parameters.
- Add `UnwrapScaleTranspose` in `CudnnScaledDotHelper::AddScaleSwizzle` to fold any preceding 2D/3D scale `kTranspose` directly into the 6D scale swizzle (`dimensions={0, 3, 1, 5, 4, 2}` instead of `{0, 1, 4, 3, 2, 5}`), avoiding a separate scale transpose kernel.
- Update `cudnn_scaled_dot_test` to expect `kSupported` on all 24 `MXFP8`, `MXFP4`, and `NVFP4` rows, add an `AUTO` entry layout test, and add the B200 benchmark and backend-verification suite.

**Compromises**
- When entry parameters have a fixed `{1, 0}` layout with major contracting dimension, `lhs` and/or `rhs` data tensors still require an explicit runtime transpose kernel before `__cudnn$fusion` because cuDNN's `BlockScaleDequantizeNode` requires unit stride on the contracting dimension.

**Alternatives**
- Relaxing contracting-dimension constraints inside `CuDnnFusionCompiler` without transposing data operands in advance fails during `CuDnnFusionCompiler::GetAvailablePlanCount` because cuDNN rejects non-unit contracting strides on block-scaled inputs.
- Canonicalizing `kScaledDot` only after `GpuLayoutAssignment` (in `BlockScalingRewriter`) works for fixed `{1, 0}` entry layouts, but misses zero-copy layout propagation when entry parameter layouts are `AUTO`.

head_commit.message:
PR #51783: Bump github/codeql-action/upload-sarif from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51783 Bumps [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add HloPipelineEditor to build HloPipelineProto.

Add HloPipelineEditor. It edits an externally owned
HloPipelineNodeSequenceProto in place. The proto is the only state.

The editor appends passes and node sequences. Each append takes an
optional max_fixed_point_iterations value. HloPassOptions supplies the pass
options. A new HloPassOptions::ToProto() writes them to the node.

display_title: [XLA] Make HloPassOptions::Get return std::optional.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Make HloPassOptions::Get return std::optional.

Replace `Get<T>(key, default_value)` with `Get<T>(key)`, which returns
`std::nullopt` for an unset option. Unset and default values are distinct both
in the proto and in pass option structs, so this keeps them symmetric: a pass
factory can apply only the options that are set (e.g. on top of base options).
A type mismatch now leaves the option unconsumed, and `CheckAllConsumed()`
reports it.

head_commit.message:
PR #51782: Bump lit from 23.1.3 to 23.1.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51782 Bumps [lit](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) from 23.1.3 to 23.1.4.
Release notes

Sourced from lit's releases.

LLVM 23.1.4 Release

  • Linux x86_64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Linux Arm64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64): xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows x64 (64-bit): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows on Arm (ARM64): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.4-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. The .tar.zst files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where LLVM-*.msi is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive clang+llvm- contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. You most likely want the LLVM- installer, unless you are developing software which itself uses LLVM, in which case choose clang+llvm-.

In addition, source archives are available:

  • To get all the llvm-project source code for this release, choose llvm-project-23.1.4.src.tar.xz.
  • test-suite-23.1.4.src.tar.xz is an archive of the LLVM Test Suite) for this release.

Verifying Packages

All packages come with a matching .sig and/or .jsonl file. You should use these to verify the integrity of the packages.

If it has a .sig file, it should have been signed by the release managers using GPG. Download the keys from the LLVM website, import them into your keyring and use them to verify the file:

$ gpg --import release-keys.asc
$ gpg --verify <package file name>.sig <package file name>

If it has a .jsonl file, use gh to verify the package:

$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name>
(if you are able to connect to GitHub)
$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name> --bundle <package file name>.jsonl
(using attestation file on disk)

PR #51783: Bump github/codeql-action/upload-sarif from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51783 Bumps [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.38.3 to 4.39.1.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

display_title: [XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate A2A+GEMM and GEMM+A2A splitting in WindowedEinsumHandler.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate A2A+GEMM and GEMM+A2A splitting in WindowedEinsumHandler.

Extract `WindowedEinsumVisitor::SplitA2aGemmAlongContractingDim` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/windowed_einsum_handler.cc` to share the contracting-dimension splitting logic between `HandleDot` (A2A+GEMM) and `HandleAllToAll` (GEMM+A2A).

The two implementations were identical except for:
- Which instruction is the root of the pattern (`dot` for A2A+GEMM vs. `a2a` for GEMM+A2A), used for the output buffer shape and final `ReplaceInstruction` call.
- Which LHS tensor is sliced in each split (`a2a->mutable_operand(0)` for A2A+GEMM vs. `dot->mutable_operand(0)` for GEMM+A2A).
- The shape and ordering of the per-split `all-to-all` and `dot` instructions (`all-to-all` with `lhs_slice_shape` followed by `dot` for A2A+GEMM vs. `dot` followed by `all-to-all` with `a2a->shape()` for GEMM+A2A).

display_title: PR #51630: [GPU] Preserve layouts when moving GEMM bitcasts

head_commit.message:
PR #51630: [GPU] Preserve layouts when moving GEMM bitcasts

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51630

Moving a bitcast across a layout-changing copy in GEMM Fusion V2 could silently drop a required data permutation. Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41952.

Only commute bitcasts when operand and result shapes and layouts agree, ignoring element type. Otherwise preserve the original operation order.

Adds numerical unit tests for both hoisting and sinking, plus an end-to-end GPU regression using the original transpose/reduce/matmul reproducer.

Validated locally: all 183 unit tests pass; the GPU regression passes with GEMM V1 and V2 on an RTX 3080. Removing the fix makes all 96 GPU output values mismatch. clang-format 17.0.6 and git diff --check pass.

display_title: PR #51351: [ROCm] Keep scaled-dot composites native through custom partitioning

head_commit.message:
PR #51351: [ROCm] Keep scaled-dot composites native through custom partitioning

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51351

When `jax.nn.scaled_matmul` runs under JAX custom partitioning on more than one device, the per-device body returned by the partition callback contains an `xla.scaled_dot` composite (on ROCm, `scaled_matmul` lowers through `lax.scaled_dot`). That composite never reaches `CompositeRewriter`: the pre-SPMD run of the pass is over by the time the callback creates it, and the callback path destroys the composite on its way into the partitioned module.

### Changes
- `CloneWithNewOperands` keeps `is_composite` on a cloned call.
- `custom_partition_callback.cc`: the callback's `CallInliner` preserves `xla.scaled_dot`, and the `composite` attributes are restored after `SpmdBuilder` derives the clone from the custom call.
- `gpu_compiler.cc`: `CompositeRewriter` runs again at the end of the SPMD pipeline, so composites created during partitioning take the same path as those rewritten before it.
- `composite_rewriter.cc`: the new `kScaledDot` keeps the call's metadata; after SPMD there is no enclosing call whose inlining would propagate an `op_name` (test added).

### Tests
- `hlo_instruction_test`, `composite_rewriter_test`, `call_inliner_test` pass.
-  end to end with MaxText on MI350X (2 to 8 GPUs, DP/FSDP/TP), all MX GEMMs compile to native `scaled-dot`, single-device HLO and loss unchanged.

display_title: [XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking in TopkSpecializer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking in TopkSpecializer.

- `BuildPackF32ToU64TotalOrder` and `BuildPackF32ToU64PartialOrder` shared the same F32-to-U32 bitwise radix flip and U64 packing logic, differing only in the reversed index bound (`0xFFFFFFFF` for `kTotal` vs. `0x7FFFFFFF` for `kPartial`) and the `-0.0f` canonicalization step for `kPartial` (shifting the 31-bit reversed index left by 1, adding `is_neg_zero` to `radix_key`, and storing `is_neg_zero` in bit 0).

head_commit.message:
PR #51351: [ROCm] Keep scaled-dot composites native through custom partitioning

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51351

When `jax.nn.scaled_matmul` runs under JAX custom partitioning on more than one device, the per-device body returned by the partition callback contains an `xla.scaled_dot` composite (on ROCm, `scaled_matmul` lowers through `lax.scaled_dot`). That composite never reaches `CompositeRewriter`: the pre-SPMD run of the pass is over by the time the callback creates it, and the callback path destroys the composite on its way into the partitioned module.

### Changes
- `CloneWithNewOperands` keeps `is_composite` on a cloned call.
- `custom_partition_callback.cc`: the callback's `CallInliner` preserves `xla.scaled_dot`, and the `composite` attributes are restored after `SpmdBuilder` derives the clone from the custom call.
- `gpu_compiler.cc`: `CompositeRewriter` runs again at the end of the SPMD pipeline, so composites created during partitioning take the same path as those rewritten before it.
- `composite_rewriter.cc`: the new `kScaledDot` keeps the call's metadata; after SPMD there is no enclosing call whose inlining would propagate an `op_name` (test added).

### Tests
- `hlo_instruction_test`, `composite_rewriter_test`, `call_inliner_test` pass.
-  end to end with MaxText on MI350X (2 to 8 GPUs, DP/FSDP/TP), all MX GEMMs compile to native `scaled-dot`, single-device HLO and loss unchanged.

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Check all instructions against register limits in indexing cost model. This massively saves on compile-time of E2E models at almost no cost on performance.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Check all instructions against register limits in indexing cost model. This massively saves on compile-time of E2E models at almost no cost on performance.

Previously, we only checked fusion boundary instructions (roots and fusion operands) and `iota` instructions. This change checks all instructions in the tiled computation: keep the `0.4 * registers_per_block_limit()` threshold for roots, fusion operands, and `iota`s, and check intermediate instructions inside the fusion against the full `registers_per_block_limit()` without the `0.4` factor (to be more relaxed).

This issue was surfaced on a `input -> broadcast -> reduce` case, where the intermediate broadcast isn't checked, yet it now requires more registers than the fusion boundaries, causing heavy spilling on certain configurations.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Match exact 16-bit rounded constants in GemmRewriter's BcastConstScalarNear

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Match exact 16-bit rounded constants in GemmRewriter's BcastConstScalarNear

In `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_rewriter.cc`, `BcastConstScalarNear`
previously used `epsilon = 128 * std::numeric_limits<T>::epsilon()` in
`std::abs(*actual - expected) < (std::abs(*actual + expected) * epsilon)`
when matching the approximate-GELU constants `sqrt(2/pi)` and `0.044715` in
`HandleMultiply`. For `BF16` (`epsilon = 1.0`), this accepted every positive
`bf16` constant in `[2^-54, 2^53]` for `c1` and `[2^-58, 2^49]` for `c2`
(13,697 of the 32,512 positive normal `bf16` values); for `F16`
(`epsilon = 0.125`), it accepted any constant within `(7/9, 9/7)` of the
expected value (`-22%` to `+29%`), causing `FuseGeluActivation` to rewrite
non-GELU `tanh` activations into cuBLASLt's `GELU` / `BIAS_GELU` epilogue.

Compare `F16` and `BF16` constants for exact equality against `expected`
rounded to `Eigen::half` / `bfloat16` while keeping the `F32` and `F64`
branches unchanged, and add `ApproxGeluActivationWrongConstantBF16` and
`ApproxGeluActivationWrongConstantF16` in `gemm_rewriter_test.cc`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

display_title: Make JAX Linux x86 AMD Instinct GPU presubmit check blocking.

head_commit.message:
Make JAX Linux x86 AMD Instinct GPU presubmit check blocking.

Over the first full 24-hour window (2026-10-28 08:23 UTC to 2026-10-29 08:23 UTC) under the 52-minute step and 55-minute job timeout cap in `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml`, `JAX Linux x86 AMD Instinct GPU` passed 145 of 153 executed PR runs (94.8%), with 7 step timeouts at 52 minutes (4.6% overall, or 3.3% excluding a 253-commit LLVM integrate), 0 test flakes, and 1 real PR build error; it also caught a real regression that XLA tests missed. Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the `jax` job in `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml` so JAX ROCm failures surface directly in workflow status and gate presubmit merges. Accepted residual risk is ~3–4% peak-hour/cold-cache timeouts due to local compilation on the 1-GPU runner; the structural follow-up is enabling remote builds via `--spawn_strategy` or scoping targets via `JAXCI_GATE_TARGETS_FILE`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1009529339

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support TF32 and BF16 F32 one-hot dot strength reduction via reduce-precision.

F32 dots round their inputs to TF32 (10 mantissa bits) or BF16 (7 mantissa bits) depending on the dot algorithm unless full F32 precision is requested.

This change uses an HLO `reduce-precision` op after the gather when strength-reducing F32 one-hot dots so the gathered weights match the dot's input rounding.

display_title: PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50406

This fixes a case where dynamic-slice fusion can leave an FFI call’s buffers in ordinary memory even though the call requests collective (symmetric) memory, `S(7)`.

Consider this structure, with a 128-element `input` and 256-element `weights` and `destination` buffers. These are schematic HLO excerpts; the attribute names and indices are exact:

```text
tile = slice(weights, [128:256])
tmp = custom_call(input, tile),
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
out = dynamic_update_slice(destination, tmp, 128)
```

The call requests collective memory for `input` and its result. Fusion replaces the temporary slices with views into their backing buffers:

```text
fused(p0_weights, p1_input, p2_destination) {
  tile = slice(p0_weights, [128:256])
  tmp = custom_call(p1_input, tile),
        frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                             results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
  return dynamic_update_slice(p2_destination, tmp, 128)
}
```

Previously, the requirements remained only on the inner call, where allocation and boundary-copy analysis could miss them:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused
```

This change puts the corresponding requirements on the outer fusion:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused,
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{1:7,2:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
```

The call’s operand `0` becomes fusion operand `1`. The destination at operand `2` also needs collective memory because the FFI now writes directly into its slice. `weights` stays in ordinary memory. Entry-boundary copies preserve ordinary-memory inputs and outputs where required.

The rewrite also preserves explicit input/output aliases. For example:

```text
tile = dynamic_slice(x, i)
updated = custom_call(tile, y)  // result aliases operand 0
out = dynamic_update_slice(x, updated, i)
```

This in-place update can fuse when the existing buffer and offset analysis proves that the aliased input and output refer to the same backing buffer and byte range. Mismatched regions, additional accesses sharing that backing buffer, or memory-space requirements that would conflict after fusion leave the call unfused.

Annotation handling is limited to custom calls and the `dynamic_slice_fusion` subtype.

Regression coverage includes operand reindexing, tuple outputs, update destinations, conflicting requests, O2 rollback, matching in-place updates, rejected overlaps, and shared collective allocation.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

temp allocated again, in the reservation"] --> b3["Profiling copy kept as stale allocator state

Over the first full 24-hour window (2026-10-28 08:23 UTC to 2026-10-29 08:23 UTC) under the 52-minute step and 55-minute job timeout cap in `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml`, `JAX Linux x86 AMD Instinct GPU` passed 145 of 153 executed PR runs (94.8%), with 7 step timeouts at 52 minutes (4.6% overall, or 3.3% excluding a 253-commit LLVM integrate), 0 test flakes, and 1 real PR build error; it also caught a real regression that XLA tests missed. Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the `jax` job in `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml` so JAX ROCm failures surface directly in workflow status and gate presubmit merges. Accepted residual risk is ~3–4% peak-hour/cold-cache timeouts due to local compilation on the 1-GPU runner; the structural follow-up is enabling remote builds via `--spawn_strategy` or scoping targets via `JAXCI_GATE_TARGETS_FILE`.

display_title: [XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

When one loop iteration reads and then updates a loop-carried buffer in place
several times in a row (e.g. gather + scatter optimizer updates of an embedding
table across unrolled loop steps), CopyInsertion adds a copy before every
in-place op and CopyRemover cannot remove any of them: in each step the copy and
the reader of the previous value are unordered, so removing one step's copy
requires the next step's reader to be ordered before the next copy, and vice
versa.

Add an opt-in CopyInsertion option that orders the other readers of an in-place
operand that are already predecessors of the in-place op before the copy added
for that operand. This does not constrain the schedule beyond what the in-place
op already requires, but gives copy removal the ordering it needs. The option is
only enabled for the TPU copy insertion pass for now.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004536340

Triton's global scratch memory allocation asserts that a module has at

single module, which aborts with `!seenKernel` when assertions are
enabled. Run each case through --split-input-file instead.

head_commit.message:
PR #50988: [XLA:GPU] Splat scalar operands in Triton atomics lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50988

#ai-generated

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50877.

## Summary of changes

Splat scalar `value` and `expected` operands to the pointer tensor shape before
creating `tt.extern_elementwise` in `LowerAtomicWriteOp` and
`LowerAtomicSpinWaitOp`. Scalar-pointer operations retain scalar operands.

Update the atomic-write and atomic-spin-wait FileCheck expectations, including
64-pointer masked cases that check the scalar splat and mask forwarding. Add a
full-pipeline regression test for a 64-rank block barrier, atomic write and
atomic spin-wait with `num-warps=1`, and remove the incorrect automatic-broadcast
comments.

## Justification

Small one-shot all-reduces over 64 devices can fail during Triton-to-LLVM
lowering with:

```text
size mismatch when packing elements for LLVM struct expected 2 but got 1
```

The block barrier passes a tensor of signal pointers and a scalar signal value
to the atomics lowering. With 64 ranks and one warp, each thread owns two
pointers, but the unsplatted scalar contributes only one value. Splatting the
value gives each pointer a corresponding operand without disabling the
collective kernel or changing its selection policy.

This was observed while compiling MaxText Llama 3.1 405B training on 64 GB200
GPUs. Thanks to @ksew1 for reporting the failure and identifying the block-barrier
atomics mechanism in #50877.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix with regression coverage.

## Regression coverage

The atomics tests check both the scalar-to-tensor splat and the unchanged mask
operand. `triton_xla_atomics_pipeline.mlir` reaches LLVM through
`--triton-xla-pipeline='target=10.0 num-warps=1'`, covering the block barrier
and both unmasked atomic operations at 64 ranks.

Mask forwarding is checked at the atomics rewrite level. A separate existing
mask-type mismatch in the CUDA extern-atomics lowering prevents an `i1`-masked
case from completing the full pipeline.

## Execution tests

### Deviceless compiler reproducer

Save this as `repro.hlo`:

```hlo
HloModule repro, num_partitions=64

add {
  a = s32[] parameter(0)
  b = s32[] parameter(1)
  ROOT r = s32[] add(a, b)
}

ENTRY main {
  p = s32[] parameter(0)
  ROOT ar = s32[] all-reduce(p), channel_id=1,
    replica_groups=[1,64]<=[64], use_global_device_ids=true, to_apply=add
}
```

From the XLA repository root, using a CUDA-enabled `hlo-opt` build:

```bash
hlo-opt repro.hlo --platform=CUDA --stage=ptx \
  --xla_gpu_topology_filename=1x16x4 \
  --xla_gpu_target_config_filename=xla/backends/gpu/target_config/specs/gb200.txtpb
```

The topology and target configuration allow compilation without allocating
64 GPUs. Repeat with `--stage=hlo` to inspect `kernel_strategy` and confirm the
Triton one-shot path. The build must provide its required CUDA runtime libraries.

The following before/after comparison was run at
[XLA 9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5](https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5)
on aarch64 with CUDA 13.5, keeping the source revision and build configuration
fixed and changing only this patch:

| Case | Unpatched | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `num_partitions=64` | Original LLVM packing error; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `replica_count=64` | Same error | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 32 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `f32[256]`, 64 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, two warps | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, cross-host one-shot disabled | Compiles using the default strategy | Compiles using the default strategy |

For the 32-device control, change `num_partitions` to 32, use
`replica_groups=[1,32]<=[32]`, and select topology `1x8x4`. For the `f32[256]`
control, use `f32[256]` for the entry parameter and all-reduce result and `f32[]`
for the reduction computation's operands and result. The disabled-path control
adds `--xla_gpu_unsupported_use_cross_host_one_shot_kernel=`.

### Training validation

A JAX CUDA plugin/jaxlib build from the same source tree with the patch completed
30 training steps for both BF16 and NVFP4 Llama 3.1 405B on 16 hosts with 4 GB200
GPUs each, with FSDP=64, sequence length 4096, and batch size 2 per device.
Cross-host one-shot remained enabled by default; no collective-kernel workaround
was used. Neither run reproduced the compiler crash.

BF16 loss matched the earlier opt-out run within 0.002 at every step, with final
loss 11.658. NVFP4 default-path runs on the same patched build ended at 10.312
and 10.439; an opt-out run on that build ended at 10.354. The observed 0.127
difference between identical-config repeats exceeds the initial 0.048 gap
between the first patched run and the earlier unpatched opt-out run (10.264).
These repeats weaken the initial numerical-regression concern, but do not
establish numerical equivalence.

### Scope of the evidence

The runtime and deviceless PTX comparisons above apply to XLA
`9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5` on aarch64/GB200.

The implementation and new full-pipeline regression test were also built and
validated at `cf8a4e9ce78d390b127abb8be17084e1d6cbba63` on aarch64 Linux with
CUDA targeting `sm_100`. Adding only the pipeline test to unpatched main
reproduces the original LLVM packing error; adding the splat change makes it
pass.

This branch is rebased onto `0cddbc999724ace276643697d2e7621d2ccf4177`.
Both patch commits are unchanged by this rebase.
The implementation and full-pipeline test match the validated versions.
The additional 64-rank masked rewrite cases were added after that validation.
Compiler, 64-GPU training and PTX comparisons have not been repeated on this base.

display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

head_commit.message:
PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50406

This fixes a case where dynamic-slice fusion can leave an FFI call’s buffers in ordinary memory even though the call requests collective (symmetric) memory, `S(7)`.

Consider this structure, with a 128-element `input` and 256-element `weights` and `destination` buffers. These are schematic HLO excerpts; the attribute names and indices are exact:

```text
tile = slice(weights, [128:256])
tmp = custom_call(input, tile),
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
out = dynamic_update_slice(destination, tmp, 128)
```

The call requests collective memory for `input` and its result. Fusion replaces the temporary slices with views into their backing buffers:

```text
fused(p0_weights, p1_input, p2_destination) {
  tile = slice(p0_weights, [128:256])
  tmp = custom_call(p1_input, tile),
        frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                             results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
  return dynamic_update_slice(p2_destination, tmp, 128)
}
```

Previously, the requirements remained only on the inner call, where allocation and boundary-copy analysis could miss them:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused
```

This change puts the corresponding requirements on the outer fusion:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused,
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{1:7,2:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
```

The call’s operand `0` becomes fusion operand `1`. The destination at operand `2` also needs collective memory because the FFI now writes directly into its slice. `weights` stays in ordinary memory. Entry-boundary copies preserve ordinary-memory inputs and outputs where required.

The rewrite also preserves explicit input/output aliases. For example:

```text
tile = dynamic_slice(x, i)
updated = custom_call(tile, y)  // result aliases operand 0
out = dynamic_update_slice(x, updated, i)
```

This in-place update can fuse when the existing buffer and offset analysis proves that the aliased input and output refer to the same backing buffer and byte range. Mismatched regions, additional accesses sharing that backing buffer, or memory-space requirements that would conflict after fusion leave the call unfused.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Preserve async ordering inside command buffers

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Preserve async fork/join ordering inside command buffers

Replace the emitter's LHS frontier bookkeeping with per-stream frontiers
keyed by execution stream, explicit async joins, nested-executor stream
ordering, and shared async execution validation.

Upstream 7f190492a9 landed the basic fork/join frontier for kLHS mode (a
main stream frontier plus a node_hash_map of async stream frontiers).
This change supersedes that bookkeeping with a single map keyed by
std::optional<ExecutionStreamId>, so a nested executor can inherit the
stream of its enclosing command, and adds on top of it:

- AsyncDoneThunk is kept as an explicit join command, including when the
  async body has no buffer dependency on subsequent commands.
- Nested executors (loops, branches, dynamic-slice fusions) report the
  streams they fork, and the enclosing command is ordered against those
  streams.
- Duplicate outstanding starts of one AsyncExecution and unmatched
  start/done pairs are rejected, matching the runtime invariant.

Tests: command_buffer_cmd_emitter_test covers fork/join reachability,
same-stream ordering, nested regions, buffer hazards, nested executors,
and validation errors. cuda_command_buffer_async_test exercises graph
creation, replay, and update on one GPU. Collective, ragged all-to-all,
and send/recv thunk tests expect the retained done join.

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

head_commit.message:
PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50406

This fixes a case where dynamic-slice fusion can leave an FFI call’s buffers in ordinary memory even though the call requests collective (symmetric) memory, `S(7)`.

Consider this structure, with a 128-element `input` and 256-element `weights` and `destination` buffers. These are schematic HLO excerpts; the attribute names and indices are exact:

```text
tile = slice(weights, [128:256])
tmp = custom_call(input, tile),
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
out = dynamic_update_slice(destination, tmp, 128)
```

The call requests collective memory for `input` and its result. Fusion replaces the temporary slices with views into their backing buffers:

```text
fused(p0_weights, p1_input, p2_destination) {
  tile = slice(p0_weights, [128:256])
  tmp = custom_call(p1_input, tile),
        frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                             results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
  return dynamic_update_slice(p2_destination, tmp, 128)
}
```

Previously, the requirements remained only on the inner call, where allocation and boundary-copy analysis could miss them:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused
```

This change puts the corresponding requirements on the outer fusion:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused,
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{1:7,2:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
```

The call’s operand `0` becomes fusion operand `1`. The destination at operand `2` also needs collective memory because the FFI now writes directly into its slice. `weights` stays in ordinary memory. Entry-boundary copies preserve ordinary-memory inputs and outputs where required.

The rewrite also preserves explicit input/output aliases. For example:

```text
tile = dynamic_slice(x, i)
updated = custom_call(tile, y)  // result aliases operand 0
out = dynamic_update_slice(x, updated, i)
```

This in-place update can fuse when the existing buffer and offset analysis proves that the aliased input and output refer to the same backing buffer and byte range. Mismatched regions, additional accesses sharing that backing buffer, or memory-space requirements that would conflict after fusion leave the call unfused.

Annotation handling is limited to custom calls and the `dynamic_slice_fusion` subtype.

Regression coverage includes operand reindexing, tuple outputs, update destinations, conflicting requests, O2 rollback, matching in-place updates, rejected overlaps, and shared collective allocation.

head_commit.message:
PR #50406: [GPU] Preserve memory-space annotations in dynamic-slice fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50406

This fixes a case where dynamic-slice fusion can leave an FFI call’s buffers in ordinary memory even though the call requests collective (symmetric) memory, `S(7)`.

Consider this structure, with a 128-element `input` and 256-element `weights` and `destination` buffers. These are schematic HLO excerpts; the attribute names and indices are exact:

```text
tile = slice(weights, [128:256])
tmp = custom_call(input, tile),
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
out = dynamic_update_slice(destination, tmp, 128)
```

The call requests collective memory for `input` and its result. Fusion replaces the temporary slices with views into their backing buffers:

```text
fused(p0_weights, p1_input, p2_destination) {
  tile = slice(p0_weights, [128:256])
  tmp = custom_call(p1_input, tile),
        frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{0:7}",
                             results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
  return dynamic_update_slice(p2_destination, tmp, 128)
}
```

Previously, the requirements remained only on the inner call, where allocation and boundary-copy analysis could miss them:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused
```

This change puts the corresponding requirements on the outer fusion:

```text
out = fusion(weights, input, destination), calls=fused,
      frontend_attributes={operands_memory_spaces="{1:7,2:7}",
                           results_memory_spaces="{0:7}"}
```

The call’s operand `0` becomes fusion operand `1`. The destination at operand `2` also needs collective memory because the FFI now writes directly into its slice. `weights` stays in ordinary memory. Entry-boundary copies preserve ordinary-memory inputs and outputs where required.

The rewrite also preserves explicit input/output aliases. For example:

```text
tile = dynamic_slice(x, i)
updated = custom_call(tile, y)  // result aliases operand 0
out = dynamic_update_slice(x, updated, i)
```

This in-place update can fuse when the existing buffer and offset analysis proves that the aliased input and output refer to the same backing buffer and byte range. Mismatched regions, additional accesses sharing that backing buffer, or memory-space requirements that would conflict after fusion leave the call unfused.

Annotation handling is limited to custom calls and the `dynamic_slice_fusion` subtype.

Regression coverage includes operand reindexing, tuple outputs, update destinations, conflicting requests, O2 rollback, matching in-place updates, rejected overlaps, and shared collective allocation.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:TPU] Prevent host offload from leaking host memory space into device while loop state and fusion operands

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TPU] Prevent host offload from leaking host memory space into device while loop state and fusion operands

In HostOffloader, WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths traverses downstream users of host offload annotations and converts device compute taking host inputs into host compute.
However:
1. When traversing through a while loop body root tuple, if an element was computed on host (e.g. arithmetic op taking a host slice) but the corresponding while loop state element was initialized on device, WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths propagated host memory space (S(5)) into the while instruction output, parameter, and while body root. This caused device-carried state to be mutated to host memory space and corrupted downstream device fusions and consumers.
2. When host memory or host compute values are consumed by device fusions (kFusion), HostOffloader did not ensure the fusion operands are transferred to device memory space, resulting in fusion parameter layout / memory space mismatches in HloVerifier.

Fix:
1. In WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths, when reaching a while body root instruction whose corresponding while state element was not initialized in host memory, insert a copy to device before the root tuple for non-DUS compute instructions and terminate the downward walk for that state element.
2. In WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths, record any kFusion successors and insert a copy to default device memory space before the fusion operand, preventing host memory space buffers from being passed into device fusion parameters.
3. Add unit tests WhileBodyHostComputeIntoDeviceStateElement and HostOffloadDoesNotFeedDeviceFusion in host_offloader_test.cc.

head_commit.message:
PR #50988: [XLA:GPU] Splat scalar operands in Triton atomics lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50988

#ai-generated

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50877.

## Summary of changes

Splat scalar `value` and `expected` operands to the pointer tensor shape before
creating `tt.extern_elementwise` in `LowerAtomicWriteOp` and
`LowerAtomicSpinWaitOp`. Scalar-pointer operations retain scalar operands.

Update the atomic-write and atomic-spin-wait FileCheck expectations, including
64-pointer masked cases that check the scalar splat and mask forwarding. Add a
full-pipeline regression test for a 64-rank block barrier, atomic write and
atomic spin-wait with `num-warps=1`, and remove the incorrect automatic-broadcast
comments.

## Justification

Small one-shot all-reduces over 64 devices can fail during Triton-to-LLVM
lowering with:

```text
size mismatch when packing elements for LLVM struct expected 2 but got 1
```

The block barrier passes a tensor of signal pointers and a scalar signal value
to the atomics lowering. With 64 ranks and one warp, each thread owns two
pointers, but the unsplatted scalar contributes only one value. Splatting the
value gives each pointer a corresponding operand without disabling the
collective kernel or changing its selection policy.

This was observed while compiling MaxText Llama 3.1 405B training on 64 GB200
GPUs. Thanks to @ksew1 for reporting the failure and identifying the block-barrier
atomics mechanism in #50877.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix with regression coverage.

## Regression coverage

The atomics tests check both the scalar-to-tensor splat and the unchanged mask
operand. `triton_xla_atomics_pipeline.mlir` reaches LLVM through
`--triton-xla-pipeline='target=10.0 num-warps=1'`, covering the block barrier
and both unmasked atomic operations at 64 ranks.

Mask forwarding is checked at the atomics rewrite level. A separate existing
mask-type mismatch in the CUDA extern-atomics lowering prevents an `i1`-masked
case from completing the full pipeline.

## Execution tests

### Deviceless compiler reproducer

Save this as `repro.hlo`:

```hlo
HloModule repro, num_partitions=64

add {
  a = s32[] parameter(0)
  b = s32[] parameter(1)
  ROOT r = s32[] add(a, b)
}

ENTRY main {
  p = s32[] parameter(0)
  ROOT ar = s32[] all-reduce(p), channel_id=1,
    replica_groups=[1,64]<=[64], use_global_device_ids=true, to_apply=add
}
```

From the XLA repository root, using a CUDA-enabled `hlo-opt` build:

```bash
hlo-opt repro.hlo --platform=CUDA --stage=ptx \
  --xla_gpu_topology_filename=1x16x4 \
  --xla_gpu_target_config_filename=xla/backends/gpu/target_config/specs/gb200.txtpb
```

The topology and target configuration allow compilation without allocating
64 GPUs. Repeat with `--stage=hlo` to inspect `kernel_strategy` and confirm the
Triton one-shot path. The build must provide its required CUDA runtime libraries.

The following before/after comparison was run at
[XLA 9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5](https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5)
on aarch64 with CUDA 13.5, keeping the source revision and build configuration
fixed and changing only this patch:

| Case | Unpatched | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `num_partitions=64` | Original LLVM packing error; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, `replica_count=64` | Same error | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 32 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, one warp | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `f32[256]`, 64 devices | Emits PTX; one-shot, two warps | Emits PTX; retains one-shot |
| `s32[]`, 64 devices, cross-host one-shot disabled | Compiles using the default strategy | Compiles using the default strategy |

For the 32-device control, change `num_partitions` to 32, use
`replica_groups=[1,32]<=[32]`, and select topology `1x8x4`. For the `f32[256]`
control, use `f32[256]` for the entry parameter and all-reduce result and `f32[]`
for the reduction computation's operands and result. The disabled-path control
adds `--xla_gpu_unsupported_use_cross_host_one_shot_kernel=`.

### Training validation

A JAX CUDA plugin/jaxlib build from the same source tree with the patch completed
30 training steps for both BF16 and NVFP4 Llama 3.1 405B on 16 hosts with 4 GB200
GPUs each, with FSDP=64, sequence length 4096, and batch size 2 per device.
Cross-host one-shot remained enabled by default; no collective-kernel workaround
was used. Neither run reproduced the compiler crash.

BF16 loss matched the earlier opt-out run within 0.002 at every step, with final
loss 11.658. NVFP4 default-path runs on the same patched build ended at 10.312
and 10.439; an opt-out run on that build ended at 10.354. The observed 0.127
difference between identical-config repeats exceeds the initial 0.048 gap
between the first patched run and the earlier unpatched opt-out run (10.264).
These repeats weaken the initial numerical-regression concern, but do not
establish numerical equivalence.

### Scope of the evidence

The runtime and deviceless PTX comparisons above apply to XLA
`9b989b5182f7c86310cd3fbd91228cc658e372e5` on aarch64/GB200.

The implementation and new full-pipeline regression test were also built and
validated at `cf8a4e9ce78d390b127abb8be17084e1d6cbba63` on aarch64 Linux with
CUDA targeting `sm_100`. Adding only the pipeline test to unpatched main
reproduces the original LLVM packing error; adding the splat change makes it
pass.

This branch is rebased onto `0cddbc999724ace276643697d2e7621d2ccf4177`.
Both patch commits are unchanged by this rebase.
The implementation and full-pipeline test match the validated versions.
The additional 64-rank masked rewrite cases were added after that validation.
Compiler, 64-GPU training and PTX comparisons have not been repeated on this base.

[XLA:CPU] Disable fast min/max by default to follow IEEE 754 signed zero semantics

Fixes tensorflow/tensorflow#128986

Disable xla_cpu_enable_fast_min_max by default on CPU (matching GPU), so that
min/max floating point reductions and elementwise operations correctly lower to
llvm.minimum / llvm.maximum intrinsics preserving IEEE 754-2019 signed zero
semantics (e.g. min(+0.0, -0.0) -> -0.0).

- Set xla_cpu_enable_fast_min_max to false with explanatory comment and updated help text.
- Add parameter-based unit tests for signed zero preservation in fmax_fmin_test and reduce_test.

- Add `LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryRegister()` and `LocalDeviceState::HostMemoryUnregister()` and use them in `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::DmaMap()`/`DmaUnmap()` and in the custom host memory allocator's `map_fn`/`unmap_fn` created by `GetStreamExecutorGpuClient()`, so that `LocalDeviceState` can control how host memory (un)registration is performed.
- Since the custom host memory allocator's `unmap_fn` now captures the first `LocalDeviceState`, explicitly destroy `host_memory_allocator_` in `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::~PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient()` while `local_device_states_` is still alive.
- Remove the redundant `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::executor_` member (always the first local device's executor) and the corresponding constructor parameters of `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient` and `StreamExecutorGpuRawClient`.

No behavior change intended.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PJRT] Add WorkerThread::IsCurrentThread().

Callers that synchronously schedule work onto a `WorkerThread` and block on a notification need a way to detect when they are already running on that thread so they can execute inline instead of deadlocking.

Track the active `WorkerThread` on each worker thread via a `thread_local` pointer in `WorkLoop()` and expose `WorkerThread::IsCurrentThread()` to check whether the caller is currently executing on a given `WorkerThread`.
